md_description: This DAG represents a dataset workflow for studying medicinal plants that produce alkaloids. It includes plant material preparation, genome sequencing, and chemical profiling, followed by computational assembly, biosynthetic gene cluster identification, locus mapping, gene annotation, metabolite annotation, and integrative analysis linking genetic loci to alkaloid products.

medicinal_plant_sample.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic sample identity and biological origin/provenance fields needed to describe the plant material before any extraction or measurement. I excluded process, capture, signal, and derivative properties because those belong to downstream nodes. I also avoided sample/subject/experiment identifiers that would be repeated elsewhere, and kept the schema focused on the minimal upstream metadata needed to interpret both genome and metabolite workflows.

md_schema.descr: Accepted taxonomic identity of the medicinal plant sample prior to any processing; use the binomial name format, for example 'Catharanthus roseus'. This is measured/recorded at sample registration and should reflect the organism from which genomic DNA and alkaloid metabolites are obtained.
Common name of the medicinal plant sample as recorded at collection or curation time, for example 'Madagascar periwinkle'. Use the vernacular name used by the study team if available.

Type of tissue collected from the plant prior to experimental manipulation, recorded at sample intake; examples include leaf, root, stem, bark, seed, flower, or whole tissue. This describes the biological source material used for both DNA extraction and chemical extraction.

Geographic origin of the plant sample as recorded at collection, using a place name, locality, or coordinates if available; for example 'Kerala, India' or '12.97, 77.59'. This helps interpret biosynthetic diversity and provenance.
Date when the plant sample was collected or acquired, recorded in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). This is the sample acquisition timepoint before any extraction or sequencing workflow.

Voucher or herbarium accession identifier for the plant specimen, if a preserved reference specimen exists; for example 'HUT-2024-0187'. Record at curation time to enable taxonomic verification and reuse.

Growth provenance of the plant sample at the time of collection, indicating whether it was field-collected, greenhouse-grown, or tissue-culture derived. Record this at sample intake because it affects genotype and metabolite interpretation.

Physical condition of the tissue at the time it entered the workflow, such as fresh, frozen, dried, or lyophilized. This is an intrinsic pre-processing sample state recorded before extraction or DNA isolation.

How the plant sample was stored prior to DNA extraction and chemical extraction, recorded at sample receipt or storage inventory; examples include liquid nitrogen, -80 C freezer, or desiccated storage. This is a sample provenance attribute, not an extraction parameter.

Whether the plant is known or expected to produce alkaloids based on prior knowledge or screening. Record at sample curation as a yes/no/unknown indicator to contextualize downstream biosynthetic and chemical analyses.

dna_extraction.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only how genomic DNA was isolated from the plant sample: extraction protocol details, reagent/kit identity, operating conditions, yield/purity, and operator/software agent context if relevant. I excluded intrinsic sample properties from the upstream Entity and excluded downstream DNA-library or sequencing outputs because those belong to later nodes. I also avoided repeating any sample identifiers already covered at the root Entity node and kept the fields specific to the extraction operation itself.

md_schema.descr: Extraction approach used to isolate genomic DNA from the plant tissue at the DNA extraction step; examples include CTAB, silica-column kit, magnetic-bead kit, or phenol-chloroform. Record the method actually applied to the sample before library preparation.

Commercial kit or in-house protocol name used for DNA isolation, recorded during the extraction operation; for example 'DNeasy Plant Mini Kit'. Use the manufacturer-branded or lab-specific name when applicable.
Kit version, protocol revision, or reagent lot-aware protocol label used for the DNA extraction procedure, recorded at run time if applicable. This helps reproduce the exact extraction conditions.

Temperature at which the DNA extraction incubation or lysis step was performed, in degrees Celsius, measured during the extraction procedure; typical plant DNA extraction ranges are about 20-65 C depending on method.

Total duration of the active extraction or lysis/incubation step, in minutes, measured from protocol start to completion for this sample. Typical values depend on the method and are often between 10 and 240 minutes.
Final elution volume used to recover purified genomic DNA, in microliters, recorded at the end of the extraction workflow; common values are 30-200 uL depending on kit and desired concentration.

Amount of purified genomic DNA recovered from the extraction, in nanograms, measured immediately after completion of the extraction and prior to library preparation; typical plant yields may range from low tens to several thousand ng.

Concentration of the extracted genomic DNA, in nanograms per microliter, measured after purification and before downstream library preparation; use the concentration from the assay used in the workflow.
Spectrophotometric DNA purity ratio A260/A280 measured after extraction and before library preparation; typical pure DNA values are around 1.8 for genomic DNA.
Qualitative assessment of extracted DNA integrity immediately after isolation and before library prep, indicating whether the DNA was suitable for downstream sequencing.

extracted_dna.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the purified DNA material after extraction and before library preparation. I excluded extraction protocol settings because they belong to the dna_extraction Process node, and I excluded library-prep or sequencing settings because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating sample identity fields and focused on the minimum DNA-quality and provenance fields a downstream user would need to assess readiness for library construction.

md_schema.descr: Type of nucleic acid material represented by this entity, recorded at post-extraction QC; for this node it should be genomic DNA intended for plant genome sequencing.
Tissue source from which the purified DNA was derived, inherited from the originating plant sample and recorded for traceability; examples include leaf, root, stem, bark, seed, or flower.

Buffer or solution in which the purified DNA is stored after extraction and before library preparation; examples include nuclease-free water, TE buffer, or elution buffer. Record the storage medium at the time the entity is handed off to library preparation.
Storage temperature of the purified DNA entity prior to library preparation, in degrees Celsius, recorded during interim storage; typical values are -20 C, -80 C, or 4 C.

Remaining amount of purified genomic DNA available for library preparation, in nanograms, measured at the handoff point from extraction QC to library prep. Typical values depend on extraction yield and consumption by QC assays.
Concentration of the purified genomic DNA available for downstream library preparation, in nanograms per microliter, measured at the post-extraction QC stage.

Instrument-derived DNA integrity score, if measured on the purified DNA entity before library preparation; use the assay-specific value such as DIN or equivalent, with the assay named in the description when available. Typical values range from 1 to 10 for DIN.

Internal inventory or tube barcode identifier for the purified DNA aliquot, recorded when the extracted DNA entity is archived or transferred to library preparation; use a stable string such as a tube barcode or lab inventory code.

sequencing_library_prep.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only library-preparation operations and settings: protocol, fragmentation and size-selection parameters, end-repair/A-tailing/adapter ligation details, PCR amplification conditions, input mass, and QC outcomes relevant to whether the library was ready for sequencing. I excluded properties of the extracted DNA entity itself and the downstream prepared library or sequencing signal, since those belong to adjacent nodes. I also avoided duplicating any fields already used for extraction, sample identity, or sequencing capture configuration.

md_schema.descr: Library construction method applied to the extracted DNA at the sequencing library prep step; examples include PCR-free, ligation-based, tagmentation-based, or in-house custom protocol. Record the actual workflow used to make the DNA sequencing-ready.
Commercial library preparation kit or protocol name used during library construction, recorded at the time of preparation; for example 'NEBNext Ultra II DNA Library Prep Kit'.
Kit version, protocol revision, or reagent lot-aware protocol label used for the sequencing library preparation, recorded during the run if applicable.

Mass of extracted DNA used as input to the library preparation reaction, in nanograms, measured at the start of the process. Typical plant genome library preparations may use from 1 ng to 1 ug depending on protocol.
Target DNA fragment length after shearing or fragmentation, in base pairs, set during library preparation; typical genome sequencing libraries may target about 200-800 bp depending on platform.
Selected library insert size range after cleanup or size selection, in base pairs, determined during library preparation; record the intended or achieved range for the sequencing-ready library.
Adapter ligation strategy used during library construction, recorded at the preparation step; examples include blunt-end ligation, TA ligation, or transposase-mediated adapter insertion.
Number of PCR amplification cycles applied to the library, measured during library preparation; 0 indicates a PCR-free workflow. Typical values are often between 4 and 18 cycles.
DNA polymerase or amplification enzyme used for library enrichment PCR, recorded during the library preparation process; for example 'KAPA HiFi HotStart'.
Total mass of sequencing-ready library recovered at the end of library preparation, in nanograms, measured before transfer to the sequencing instrument.
Whether the prepared library passed the quality-control criteria required for sequencing handoff, recorded at the end of the library preparation process; use this to indicate sequencing readiness.

prepared_dna_library.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the sequencing-ready DNA library after preparation and before capture. I excluded library prep protocol parameters because those belong to the sequencing_library_prep Process node, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to genome_sequencing Capture. I also avoided duplicating sample and extraction provenance, focusing on library identity, composition, and readiness traits needed by downstream sequencing users.

md_schema.descr: Material type represented by this entity, recorded after library construction and before sequencing; for this node it should be a genomic DNA sequencing library.
Unique barcode or tube identifier assigned to the prepared library aliquot, recorded at handoff to sequencing. Use a stable string such as a plate barcode or lab inventory code.

Observed or expected DNA insert size in base pairs for the prepared library, measured after library QC and before sequencing. Typical plant genome libraries may fall around 200-800 bp depending on protocol.
Concentration of the prepared sequencing library in nanograms per microliter, measured immediately before loading onto the sequencing instrument.
Total mass of library DNA available for sequencing, in nanograms, measured at the handoff stage from library prep to capture.
Whether sequencing adapters are successfully present on the prepared library molecules, assessed during post-prep QC before sequencing.
Qualitative assessment of the prepared library purity at the sequencing-ready stage, indicating whether the material is suitable for genome sequencing.
Storage condition of the prepared library before sequencing, recorded at the time of transfer or interim storage; examples include 4 C, -20 C, or dry ice.

genome_sequencing.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration for genome sequencing: platform identity, manufacturer/model/serial context, run structure, chemistry, read configuration, loading and basecalling settings, and run-level QC indicators. I excluded DNA library properties because those belong to the prepared_dna_library Entity, and I excluded file-format or read-file properties because those belong to the raw_genome_reads Signal. I also avoided process-like library construction settings and kept the schema focused on actively configured capture parameters and instrument descriptors.

md_schema.descr: Sequencing technology used to measure the prepared DNA library during this capture session; record the platform class actually used for the run, for example Illumina short-read sequencing. This is recorded at instrument configuration time.
Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for genome sequencing, recorded as part of the capture session configuration; for example 'Illumina'.
Model name of the sequencing instrument used in this capture session; for example 'NovaSeq 6000'. Record the exact model used to generate the raw reads.
Instrument serial number used for the sequencing session, recorded at capture time for traceability; use the serial printed on the sequencing system or asset record.
Sequencing run identifier assigned to the capture session, for example a flow-cell or run barcode such as 'Run12345'. Record this at the start of the sequencing session.

Flow cell or chip identifier used in the sequencing instrument for this capture session, recorded before and/or during the run. Use the platform-specific identifier as printed by the instrument or reagent packaging.
Sequencing chemistry or kit version used during the run, recorded at instrument setup; for example v1.5 chemistry or a platform-specific reagent kit name.
Read structure configured for the sequencing run, recorded as paired-end or single-end and, when applicable, the read lengths. Typical examples include paired-end 150 bp or single-end 100 bp.
Lane number used on the flow cell or array when the library was loaded for sequencing, recorded during run setup; use 1-based indexing if the platform supports lanes.
Final loading concentration of the prepared DNA library on the sequencing instrument, in picomoles, recorded at run setup before data acquisition. Typical values depend on platform and chemistry.
Observed cluster density for short-read patterned or non-patterned flow cells, in thousands of clusters per square millimeter, measured during the sequencing run or final run report when applicable.
Total duration of the sequencing run, in hours, measured from run start to completion for this capture session. Typical runs may last from a few hours to multiple days depending on platform.

Software used by the instrument or pipeline to convert raw instrument signals into sequence reads, recorded as part of the capture session configuration if basecalling is performed inline; for example 'Illumina RTA' or a vendor basecaller.
Whether the sequencing capture session met the instrument run quality thresholds required to produce usable raw reads, assessed at the end of the run.

raw_genome_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw data artefact properties: file formats, read counts/sizes, read length/dimensions, technical quality metrics, and storage location. I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the genome_sequencing Capture node, and I excluded assembly or biological interpretation because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating library or sample provenance fields already defined upstream.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw genome read artefact produced by the sequencing capture step; examples include FASTQ, BCL, or vendor-native signal containers. Record the format as stored in the dataset.

Whether the raw reads are stored as single-end or paired-end files, recorded from the raw data artefact structure rather than the sequencing setup. Use this to describe the organization of the files delivered to downstream analysis.
Total number of reads or read pairs in the raw genome read file set, counted after sequencing output generation and before assembly. This is a file-level size metric for the raw signal artefact.

Total number of sequenced bases represented by the raw genome reads, in bases, measured from the file contents after capture. Typical whole-genome plant datasets may range from millions to billions of bases.

Nominal read length in base pairs contained in the raw sequence files, recorded from the raw read artefact dimensions; for paired-end data, report the per-read length. Common values include 50, 100, 150, or longer depending on platform.
Total file size of the raw genome read artefact, in bytes, measured from the stored data files after sequencing. This is a technical property of the raw signal output.

Mean base-calling quality score across the raw genome read file set, calculated from the raw reads and recorded as a technical quality metric of the signal artefact. Typical Illumina values are often in the high 20s to 30s.

Percentage of bases in the raw reads with Phred quality score of at least Q30, computed from the raw signal output as a technical quality indicator. Higher values indicate better raw sequencing quality.
Estimated percentage of reads or bases containing adapter sequence contamination in the raw read artefact, measured from post-run QC on the signal files.

File system path, object-store URI, or repository location where the raw genome read files are stored, recorded after capture for data access. Examples include '/data/runs/run123/reads.fastq.gz' or 's3://bucket/path/'.

genome_assembly.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only assembly-method and computation settings: assembler identity, version, algorithm parameters, read preprocessing assumptions, compute environment, and assembly-quality indicators produced at the end of the process. I excluded raw-read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal, and I excluded assembly outputs such as contigs/scaffolds because those belong to the downstream assembled_genome Derivative. I also avoided duplicating sequencing capture settings and sample provenance.

md_schema.descr: Genome assembler used to computationally assemble the raw reads, recorded for this process step; for example 'SPAdes', 'Canu', or 'Flye'. Use the actual assembly tool applied to the plant genome data.
Version of the assembly software used for this process, recorded at run time to support reproducibility; for example '3.15.5'.

Software repository, package source, or code provenance for the assembler used in this process step, recorded to identify the exact implementation; for example a GitHub URL, Conda package source, or vendor distribution.
Assembly mode or strategy selected for the genome assembly process, recorded during configuration; examples include short-read de novo, hybrid, or long-read assembly.

k-mer size used by the assembler or assembly pipeline, recorded as a process parameter when applicable; typical values depend on the tool and read length, often between 21 and 127 for short-read assembly.

Minimum contig length threshold used or reported by the assembly process, in base pairs, recorded as a process setting for downstream filtering or reporting. Typical thresholds may range from 200 bp to 1000 bp or more.
Whether raw reads were error-corrected as part of the assembly process before contig generation, recorded during workflow execution.

Approximate genome coverage of the raw reads used for assembly, expressed as fold coverage, recorded at assembly time to contextualize completeness and contiguity. Typical plant genome coverage values may range from 20x to 200x or higher.
Compute environment used to run the assembly process, recorded for reproducibility; examples include local workstation, HPC cluster, or cloud instance.
Wall-clock time required to complete the assembly process, in hours, measured from job start to completion.
Qualitative outcome of the assembly process at completion, indicating whether the resulting assembly met internal quality thresholds before being handed to the assembled_genome derivative.

assembled_genome.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed assembly output properties: contiguity, completeness, size, scaffold counts, ambiguity metrics, and other scientific quality indicators describing the assembled genome itself. I excluded assembly software and parameter settings because those belong to the genome_assembly Process node, and I excluded raw-read properties because those belong upstream to the Signal node. I also avoided repeating sample provenance fields and focused on the assembly artifact characteristics downstream users need for gene and BGC analysis.

md_schema.descr: Representation format of the computed genome assembly, recorded for the derived assembly artifact; examples include contigs only, scaffolds, or chromosome-scale pseudomolecules.
File format used to store the genome assembly artifact, recorded when the derivative is written to disk; for example FASTA, gzipped FASTA, or an assembly graph format.
Total length of all assembled sequences in the genome assembly, in base pairs, measured on the derived assembly output. Typical values should approximate the expected plant genome size.
Number of contigs or scaffolds in the assembled genome, counted from the derived assembly artifact after computational assembly. Lower counts generally indicate more contiguous assemblies.
N50 contig or scaffold length of the assembled genome, in base pairs, calculated from the final assembly output as a contiguity metric. Higher values indicate longer assembled sequences.
L50 count of the assembled genome, meaning the number of contigs or scaffolds needed to cover 50 percent of the assembly length, calculated from the final assembly output.
GC content of the assembled genome, expressed as percent of bases that are G or C, calculated from the final assembly artifact.

Estimated completeness of the derived assembly, expressed as a percent from an assembly assessment method such as BUSCO or a comparable metric. Record the score associated with the final assembly artifact.
Percentage of expected single-copy orthologs recovered as complete in the assembled genome, measured on the final assembly artifact using BUSCO or a similar benchmark.
Percentage of expected orthologs recovered as fragmented in the assembled genome, measured on the final assembly artifact using BUSCO or a similar benchmark.
Percentage of expected orthologs missing from the assembled genome, measured on the final assembly artifact using BUSCO or a similar benchmark.
Percent of ambiguous or unresolved bases in the derived assembly, typically represented by N characters, calculated from the final assembly output as a technical quality indicator.

Accession or repository identifier assigned to the assembled genome artifact, for example a GenBank/ENA/DDBJ accession or internal assembly accession. Record the identifier attached to the finished assembly output.

gene_prediction.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the gene-prediction workflow settings and model/protocol details: prediction software, version, species/model configuration, training evidence, thresholds, and a run-level QC outcome. I excluded assembly properties because those belong to the upstream assembled_genome Derivative, and I excluded the predicted gene set output because that belongs to the downstream predicted_genes Derivative. I also avoided duplicating generic software-agent metadata unless it is necessary to specify the prediction model used in this process.

md_schema.descr: Gene prediction software used to infer protein-coding genes from the assembled genome, recorded for this process step; for example 'AUGUSTUS', 'GeneMark', or 'BRAKER'.
Version of the gene prediction software used in this process, recorded at run time for reproducibility; for example '3.5.0'.
Software repository or implementation source used for gene prediction, recorded to identify the exact codebase or package; for example a GitHub URL, Conda package source, or vendor distribution.

Operating mode used by the gene predictor at this process step, indicating whether predictions were made ab initio, evidence-guided, or combined. This is recorded during configuration of the gene prediction run.
Species model or training organism used to parameterize the gene predictor, recorded during the process; for example a closely related plant species or a custom training set name.
Source of evidence used to train or guide gene prediction, recorded for this process step; examples include RNA-seq, protein homology, or a curated gene set.
Maximum intron length allowed by the prediction model during gene calling, in base pairs, recorded as a process parameter. Typical values vary by species and predictor.
Confidence or score cutoff used to accept predicted genes from the model, recorded during gene prediction; the exact scale depends on the software and should match the run configuration.
Number of gene models predicted during the process before downstream filtering and formatting, recorded as a process outcome summary. This helps assess prediction scale and parameter effects.
Qualitative assessment of the gene prediction run at completion, indicating whether the predictions were considered suitable for downstream cluster analysis.

predicted_genes.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only output properties of the predicted gene set: file/annotation format, gene model counts, sequence/model dimensions, coverage of the assembly by predictions, and quality indicators describing the derived result. I excluded gene-prediction software, training, and thresholds because those belong to the upstream gene_prediction Process node, and I excluded assembly properties because those belong to the assembled_genome Derivative. I also avoided reusing sample or sequencing identifiers and kept the fields focused on the gene-catalog artifact itself.

md_schema.descr: File or annotation format used for the derived predicted gene set, recorded when the gene models are written out; examples include GFF3, GTF, and BED-like annotation tables.
Total number of candidate protein-coding genes in the derived gene set, counted after prediction and any basic formatting/filtering applied to the output artifact.
Total number of predicted transcript models associated with the derived gene set, if the output includes transcript isoforms. Record the count in the final gene annotation artifact.
Total number of exons represented across the predicted gene models in the derived output, counted from the final gene set artifact.
Mean length of predicted gene models, in base pairs, calculated from the derived gene set at the time it is exported or summarized. Typical values depend on the plant lineage and annotation strategy.
Number of predicted genes per megabase of assembled genome sequence, calculated from the derived gene set and the associated assembly length. This is a summary property of the output artifact.
Estimated percent of the assembled genome covered by predicted gene models, calculated from the derived annotation output as a quality and completeness indicator.
Qualitative assessment of whether the predicted gene set is sufficiently complete for downstream biosynthetic cluster analysis, evaluated on the final derivative artifact.
Accession or internal identifier assigned to the predicted gene set artifact, such as a GFF3 release tag or repository accession. Record the identifier attached to the finished derivative output.

bgc_identification.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only BGC-identification workflow parameters and software context: the tool used, version/repository, search mode, cutoff thresholds, cluster size constraints, detection database, and a run-level QC outcome. I excluded assembly and gene-set properties because those belong to upstream derivatives, and I excluded the identified clusters themselves because those belong to the downstream biosynthetic_gene_clusters derivative. I also avoided duplicating generic software fields unless needed to specify the exact BGC detection implementation.

md_schema.descr: Software used to identify biosynthetic gene clusters from the predicted genes and assembly context, recorded for this process step; for example 'antiSMASH', 'DeepBGC', or a custom pipeline.
Version of the BGC detection software used in this process, recorded at run time for reproducibility; for example '7.0.0'.
Software repository or implementation source used for BGC identification, recorded to identify the exact codebase or package; for example a GitHub URL, Conda package source, or vendor distribution.
Mode of BGC detection used in this process, indicating whether clusters were detected de novo, by rule-based screening, or by hybrid evidence integration.
Minimum genomic span required for a candidate biosynthetic gene cluster to be reported by the identification process, in base pairs, recorded as a process parameter.
Maximum allowed intergene or inter-feature gap within a candidate biosynthetic gene cluster, in base pairs, recorded during configuration of the detection process.
HMM or reference database used by the detection workflow to classify biosynthetic domains or cluster types, recorded at process time; for example PFAM, TIGRFAM, or a custom BGC database.
Score or confidence threshold used to accept a predicted biosynthetic gene cluster, recorded for this process step. The numeric scale depends on the tool and should match the configured cutoff.
Number of candidate biosynthetic gene clusters identified by the process before downstream locus mapping or curation, recorded as a process summary statistic.
Qualitative assessment of whether the BGC identification run completed successfully and produced usable clusters for downstream analyses.

biosynthetic_gene_clusters.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only output properties of the derived cluster catalog: file/record format, cluster counts, sizes and organization, genomic span, confidence/scoring summaries, and quality indicators describing the resulting cluster set. I excluded BGC detection software and thresholds because those belong to the upstream bgc_identification Process node, and I excluded the underlying assembly and gene set properties because those belong to upstream derivatives. I also avoided repeating identifiers already assigned at the root or elsewhere and focused on the cluster artifact itself.

md_schema.descr: File or record format used to store the derived biosynthetic gene cluster catalog, recorded when the output artifact is produced; examples include GFF3, TSV, JSON, or BED-like cluster tables.
Total number of candidate biosynthetic gene clusters in the derived catalog, counted after identification and any basic output curation.
Summary of cluster classes present in the derived catalog, recorded as a compact string or encoded summary; for example NRPS, PKS, terpene, alkaloid-associated, or mixed cluster classes.
Mean genomic length of the candidate biosynthetic gene clusters, in base pairs, calculated from the derived catalog. Typical cluster spans may range from a few kilobases to tens of kilobases.
Length of the largest candidate biosynthetic gene cluster in the derived catalog, in base pairs, calculated from the output artifact.
Percentage of candidate clusters in the derived catalog that contain at least one match to a known biosynthetic domain or reference profile, calculated from the output annotation.

Mean confidence score assigned to the clusters in the derived catalog, calculated from the identification output. The exact scale depends on the upstream tool but should be consistent within the dataset.
Qualitative summary of whether the derived cluster catalog contains likely novel clusters not matching known references, assessed from the final output artifact.
Accession or internal identifier assigned to the biosynthetic gene cluster catalog artifact, such as a repository release tag or internal catalog code.

locus_mapping.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the locus-mapping operation details: mapping method, software/pipeline, version, coordinate system, anchoring and overlap thresholds, and a run-level QC outcome. I excluded the cluster catalog itself and the final mapped locus table because those belong to the upstream biosynthetic_gene_clusters derivative and downstream cluster_locus_map derivative, respectively. I also avoided repeating assembly properties except where needed as inputs to the mapping operation and kept the fields focused on how loci were determined.

md_schema.descr: Method used to map identified biosynthetic gene clusters back onto genomic coordinates, recorded for this process step; examples include sequence alignment, interval overlap, or custom coordinate projection.
Software or pipeline used to perform locus mapping from clusters to genomic coordinates, recorded at process time; for example a custom bioinformatics pipeline or genome browser utility.
Version of the locus-mapping software or pipeline used in this process, recorded for reproducibility; for example '1.2.0'.
Repository or implementation source for the locus-mapping method, recorded to identify the exact codebase or script collection used in this process step.

Coordinate convention used when mapping clusters onto the genome, recorded during this process; for example 1-based closed intervals or 0-based half-open intervals. This affects locus interpretation downstream.

Minimum percent identity required for a cluster-to-genome mapping to be accepted, recorded as a process parameter when sequence alignment is used. Typical thresholds may range from 80 to 100 percent depending on strategy.
Minimum percent coverage required for a cluster-to-genome mapping to be retained, recorded at process configuration. This threshold defines how much of the cluster must align to the target locus.
Confidence threshold required to designate a genomic interval as the cluster locus, recorded during mapping. The scale depends on the mapping method and should match the run configuration.
Number of biosynthetic gene clusters successfully mapped to genomic loci by the process, recorded as a process outcome summary.
Qualitative assessment of whether the locus mapping run produced usable genomic coordinates for downstream integrative analysis.

cluster_locus_map.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only properties of the computed locus map output: representation format, genomic coordinate conventions, mapped locus counts, span/position summaries, contig/chromosome distribution, and quality indicators for the derived map. I excluded locus-mapping software and thresholds because those belong to the upstream locus_mapping Process node, and I excluded the original cluster catalog and assembly details because those belong to upstream derivatives. I also avoided repeating identifiers from the root or other nodes and focused on the locus map artifact itself.

md_schema.descr: File or record format used to store the derived cluster locus map, recorded when the output artifact is produced; examples include GFF3, BED, TSV, or JSON.
Coordinate convention used in the derived locus map, recorded with the artifact for correct interpretation; for example 1-based closed or 0-based half-open intervals.
Total number of biosynthetic gene cluster loci represented in the derived locus map, counted from the output artifact after mapping and any basic curation.
Genomic span covered by the mapped cluster loci in the derived locus map, in base pairs, measured from the final artifact as a summary of mapped interval extent.
Number of contigs or scaffolds in the assembled genome that contain at least one mapped cluster locus, counted from the derived locus map output.
Number of mapped biosynthetic cluster loci per megabase of assembled genome sequence, calculated from the derived locus map artifact.
Estimated percentage of identified clusters that were successfully placed onto genomic coordinates in the derived map, calculated as a completeness indicator for the final artifact.
Qualitative assessment of whether any cluster loci in the derived map remain ambiguous or multiply placed, evaluated on the final output artifact.
Accession or internal identifier assigned to the derived cluster locus map artifact, such as a repository release tag or internal map code.

gene_annotation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the annotation workflow details: annotation software, version, repository, reference databases, evidence types, thresholds, and run-level QC. I excluded the cluster gene set itself because that belongs to the upstream biosynthetic_gene_clusters derivative, and I excluded the annotated output table because that belongs to the downstream annotated_cluster_genes derivative. I also avoided duplicating generic software metadata unless needed to specify the exact annotation implementation and its inputs.

md_schema.descr: Software used to functionally annotate cluster genes and assign biosynthetic roles, recorded for this process step; for example 'InterProScan', 'eggNOG-mapper', or a custom annotation pipeline.
Version of the gene annotation software used in this process, recorded at run time for reproducibility; for example '5.66-98.0'.
Repository or implementation source used for gene annotation, recorded to identify the exact codebase or package; for example a GitHub URL, Conda package source, or vendor distribution.

Reference database used during cluster gene annotation, recorded as part of the process inputs; examples include InterPro, Pfam, KEGG, or UniProt. Use the database most central to the functional assignment.
Version or release date of the reference database used for gene annotation, recorded at process time for reproducibility.
Type of evidence used to assign function to cluster genes in this process, recorded during annotation; examples include domain matches, homology, motifs, or curated orthology.
Minimum domain or annotation score required to assign a functional role to a cluster gene, recorded as a process parameter; the exact scale depends on the annotation tool.
Maximum acceptable E-value threshold used for annotation hit acceptance, recorded during the gene annotation process. Typical values may range from 1e-3 to 1e-20 depending on stringency.
Number of cluster genes successfully assigned a functional annotation by the process, recorded as an outcome summary.
Qualitative assessment of whether the annotation run produced usable functional assignments for downstream pathway analysis.

annotated_cluster_genes.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only output-table properties of the annotated gene set: file format, row counts, number of unique genes and functions, coverage of the cluster set, evidence composition, and annotation confidence/quality indicators. I excluded annotation software, databases, and thresholds because those belong to the upstream gene_annotation Process node, and I excluded the unannotated gene cluster catalog because that belongs upstream to biosynthetic_gene_clusters. I also avoided repeating identifiers already defined elsewhere and focused on the final annotation artifact.

md_schema.descr: File or table format used to store the derived cluster gene annotation output, recorded when the artifact is written; examples include TSV, CSV, JSON, or GFF3-derived attribute tables.
Total number of rows in the derived annotation table, counted after annotation and formatting. This may exceed gene count if multiple functional hits are recorded per gene.
Number of unique cluster genes present in the derived annotation table, counted from the final output artifact.
Number of distinct predicted biochemical functions assigned across the derived annotation table, counted from the final output artifact.
Percentage of cluster genes from the input cluster catalog that received at least one functional annotation in the derived table, calculated from the final annotation artifact.
Percentage of annotated genes assigned to biosynthetic or enzyme-related functions rather than generic or hypothetical functions, calculated from the final table as an interpretive summary.

Mean confidence score or comparable summary statistic for the functional assignments in the derived table, calculated from the final annotation output. The exact scale depends on the upstream annotation software.
Fraction of entries in the derived annotation table labeled as hypothetical or uncharacterized proteins, calculated from the final output as a quality indicator for annotation depth.
Accession or internal identifier assigned to the derived annotation table artifact, such as a repository release tag or internal table code.

plant_extraction.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only extraction-operation details for the metabolite workflow: extraction method, solvent composition, ratio, temperature/time, agitation, cleanup, and extract QC. I excluded intrinsic sample provenance from the upstream plant sample Entity and excluded the prepared extract’s storage/file properties because those belong to the downstream prepared_plant_extract Entity. I also avoided repeating DNA-related extraction fields and kept the schema focused on how the chemical extract was produced for alkaloid profiling.

md_schema.descr: Extraction approach used to recover alkaloid metabolites from the plant tissue, recorded for this process step; examples include maceration, sonication, Soxhlet, microwave-assisted extraction, or solid-liquid extraction.
Primary solvent or solvent mixture used during plant extraction, recorded at the start of the process; examples include methanol, ethanol, water, chloroform, or methanol-water mixtures.

Percent composition of the primary extraction solvent in the solvent mixture, recorded during process setup; for example 70 percent methanol or 80 percent ethanol. Use this when a mixed solvent system is applied.

Volume of extraction solvent used per gram of plant tissue, in milliliters per gram, measured or configured during the extraction process. Typical ratios are often between 5 and 50 mL/g depending on tissue and method.

Temperature at which the plant extraction was performed, in degrees Celsius, measured during the extraction process; common values range from room temperature to about 80 C depending on the method and target metabolites.
Total duration of the plant extraction, in minutes, measured from initiation to completion of the metabolite recovery step.
Type of agitation or mixing applied during extraction, recorded as part of the process conditions; examples include shaking, stirring, vortexing, or static incubation.
Cleanup or enrichment method applied to the crude extract during the process, recorded when used; examples include filtration, centrifugation, SPE, or protein precipitation.
Mass of crude plant extract recovered at the end of the extraction process, in milligrams, measured after solvent removal or concentration as appropriate.
Qualitative assessment of whether the prepared extract met criteria for downstream chemical profiling, recorded at the end of the extraction process.

prepared_plant_extract.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared extract as a material ready for metabolite analysis: matrix/source, solvent composition, concentration, storage, aliquot identity, and readiness/stability traits. I excluded extraction protocol settings because those belong to the plant_extraction Process node, and I excluded metabolite measurement settings because those belong to metabolite_profiling Capture. I also avoided repeating the original plant sample identifiers and kept the fields focused on the extract entity itself.

md_schema.descr: Material type represented by this entity, recorded after extraction and before chemical analysis; for this node it should be a plant metabolite extract.
Plant tissue type from which the extract was derived, inherited from the source sample and recorded for traceability; examples include leaf, root, stem, bark, seed, or flower.
Solvent or solvent mixture retained in the prepared extract entity, recorded after extraction and concentration steps; for example methanol, ethanol, methanol-water, or aqueous buffer.
Concentration of the prepared plant extract, in milligrams per milliliter, measured at the handoff point to chemical analysis. Typical values depend on concentration and reconstitution steps.
Volume of the extract aliquot prepared for analysis, in microliters, recorded when the extract is portioned for chemical characterization.
Storage temperature of the prepared extract prior to chemical analysis, in degrees Celsius, recorded at sample storage or transfer; common values are -20 C or -80 C.
Number of days the prepared extract was stored before chemical analysis, measured from extract preparation to profiling. This helps interpret stability-sensitive alkaloids.
Unique vial or aliquot barcode assigned to the prepared extract entity, recorded at the time of transfer to chemical analysis; use a stable internal sample identifier.
Qualitative assessment of whether the prepared extract is expected to remain chemically stable for analysis, based on storage and handling conditions at the entity stage.

metabolite_profiling.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I kept only metabolite-profiling session and instrument-configuration fields, but I removed the collided field names previously generated elsewhere in the DAG: instrument_manufacturer, instrument_model, instrument_serial_number, and run_qc_pass. The revised schema still captures the active measurement configuration, acquisition settings, and run-quality context using non-duplicative field names specific to this node.

md_schema.descr: Analytical chemistry platform used to measure the plant extract during this capture session; record the instrument class actually used, for example LC-MS/MS, GC-MS, or NMR. This is recorded at instrument configuration time.
Ionization mode configured for the capture session, recorded for mass-spectrometry-based metabolite profiling; common values include positive or negative ionization.
Mass analyzer type or equivalent detection module used in the instrument, recorded during capture setup; examples include quadrupole, orbitrap, time-of-flight, or ion trap.
Chromatography column or separation module used during metabolite profiling, recorded as an active instrument configuration parameter; for example C18 reversed-phase column name and dimensions.
Data acquisition mode configured for the run, recorded during the capture session; examples include full scan, targeted, data-dependent acquisition, or data-independent acquisition.
Mass-to-charge scan range configured for the instrument during metabolite profiling, recorded as the acquisition window; for example 50-1500 m/z. This is measured/configured at run setup.
Collision energy used for fragmentation during MS/MS acquisition, in electronvolts, recorded during instrument setup. Typical values depend on platform and acquisition strategy.
Whether an internal standard or standard mixture was included in the metabolite-profiling capture session, recorded at instrument setup for quantitative quality control.
Whether the analytical instrument was calibrated or tuned before the capture session, recorded as part of the run setup to ensure data quality.
Qualitative assessment of whether the metabolite-profiling capture session met the quality criteria required to produce usable raw metabolomic data, assessed at the end of the run.

raw_metabolite_spectra.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw-data artefact properties for the metabolomics output: file format, dimensionality, acquisition channels, size, technical quality metrics, and storage location. I excluded capture settings such as instrument/manufacturer/model because those belong to the metabolite_profiling Capture node, and I excluded processed features or chemical interpretation because those belong downstream. I also avoided the already_generated fields flagged as collisions and kept the schema focused on the raw spectral files themselves.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw metabolite spectra artefact produced by the capture session; examples include mzML, mzXML, netCDF, or vendor-native raw files. Record the stored format of the raw signal data.
Total number of spectra or scans contained in the raw metabolite spectra file set, counted after acquisition and before processing. This is a raw signal size metric.
Total number of MS1 and MS2 scans represented in the raw spectral file set, counted from the stored spectra artifact. If only one scan level is present, report that count accordingly.
Lower bound of the mass-to-charge range represented in the raw spectral data, measured in m/z from the stored raw signal artifact; typical metabolomics acquisitions may start near 50 m/z.

Upper bound of the mass-to-charge range represented in the raw spectral data, measured in m/z from the stored raw signal artifact; typical metabolomics acquisitions may extend to 1000-2000 m/z depending on platform.
Chromatographic retention time window covered by the raw spectra, in minutes, measured from the stored raw signal artifact for LC-based profiling.
Total file size of the raw metabolite spectra artefact, in bytes, measured from the stored file after acquisition. This is a technical property of the raw signal output.

Approximate spectral resolution of the raw metabolite data, if applicable to the platform, recorded as a technical property of the signal artifact; use the instrument-reported value or equivalent summary.
Mean signal-to-noise ratio across the raw spectral file set, calculated as a technical quality metric of the raw metabolite spectra.
Estimated mass accuracy of the raw metabolite spectra, expressed in parts per million, computed from the raw signal as a technical quality indicator.

File system path, object-store URI, or repository location where the raw metabolite spectra files are stored, recorded after capture for data access. Examples include '/data/mzml/run1.mzML' or 's3://bucket/path/'.

spectral_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only spectral-processing operation details: software, version, repository, peak-detection/deconvolution settings, alignment and normalization choices, filtering thresholds, and a run-level processing QC summary. I excluded raw spectral file properties because those belong upstream to the raw_metabolite_spectra Signal, and I excluded feature-table output properties because those belong to the downstream processed_metabolite_features Derivative. I also avoided the previously generated collision fields and kept the schema specific to how raw spectra were transformed into processed features.

md_schema.descr: Software used to process raw metabolite spectra into detected features and cleaned chromatographic profiles, recorded for this process step; for example 'MZmine', 'XCMS', or 'MS-DIAL'.
Version of the spectral processing software used in this process, recorded at run time for reproducibility; for example '3.0', '4.2', or a pipeline release tag.
Repository or implementation source used for spectral processing, recorded to identify the exact codebase or package; for example a GitHub URL, Conda package source, or vendor distribution.
Peak detection or peak picking method used to extract features from the raw spectra, recorded during processing; examples include local minimum, centroid, or wavelet-based detection.
Whether retention-time alignment was applied during spectral processing to correct chromatographic shifts across samples, recorded as a process setting.
Maximum retention-time deviation tolerated during alignment, in minutes, recorded as a process parameter when alignment is enabled. Typical values are often in the range of 0.05 to 1.0 minutes.
Minimum intensity threshold used to retain detected spectral features during processing, recorded as a process cutoff. The numeric scale depends on the instrument and preprocessing pipeline.
Method used to reduce background noise or baseline artifacts during spectral processing, recorded as part of the workflow; examples include smoothing, baseline correction, or denoising.
Normalization method applied to the processed spectral features, recorded during processing; examples include TIC normalization, internal-standard normalization, or quantile normalization.
Estimated number of detected features produced by the processing run, recorded as a process summary before the feature table is handed off to the derivative node.
Qualitative assessment of whether the spectral-processing run produced usable cleaned features for downstream annotation, recorded at process completion.

processed_metabolite_features.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only output-table properties of the processed metabolite features: file format, feature counts, dimensionality, retention-time/mass summaries, coverage and sparsity indicators, and technical quality metrics describing the derived feature table itself. I excluded spectral-processing software and parameters because those belong to the upstream spectral_processing Process node, and I excluded chemical identity assignments because those belong downstream to alkaloid_annotation. I also avoided the already-generated collision fields and kept the schema focused on the feature table artifact.

md_schema.descr: File or table format used to store the derived metabolite feature table, recorded when the output artifact is written; examples include CSV, TSV, mzTab, or Parquet.
Total number of chromatographic or spectral features detected in the derived metabolite feature table, counted after processing and any basic curation.
Number of detected features flagged as putatively alkaloid-related in the derived feature table, counted from the final output artifact.
Number of quantitative dimensions represented for each feature in the derived table, such as m/z, retention time, and intensity. Record the actual dimensionality of the output artifact.
Lower bound of the mass-to-charge values represented among the derived features, measured from the final feature table; typical metabolomics feature sets may begin near 50 m/z.
Upper bound of the mass-to-charge values represented among the derived features, measured from the final feature table; typical values depend on the acquisition range and filtering.
Chromatographic retention-time span covered by the derived features, in minutes, measured from the final feature table for LC-based workflows.
Percentage of feature values missing across the derived table, calculated as a sparsity or completeness metric for the processed metabolite feature set.
Overall technical quality score for the derived feature table, calculated or assigned after spectral processing and before annotation. Use the score reported with the final output artifact.
Accession or internal identifier assigned to the processed metabolite feature table artifact, such as a repository release tag or internal table code.

alkaloid_annotation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only annotation-workflow details for assigning alkaloid identities: software, version, repository, reference library/database, matching mode, mass/tolerance thresholds, confidence cutoffs, and a run-level QC outcome. I excluded the processed feature table itself because that belongs upstream to processed_metabolite_features, and I excluded the annotated alkaloid output because that belongs to the downstream annotated_alkaloids derivative. I also avoided the already-generated collision fields and kept the schema focused on how identities were assigned from reference knowledge.

md_schema.descr: Software used to assign alkaloid identities to processed metabolite features, recorded for this process step; for example 'Compound Discoverer', 'MS-FINDER', or a custom annotation pipeline.
Version of the alkaloid annotation software used in this process, recorded at run time for reproducibility; for example '3.3'.
Repository or implementation source used for alkaloid annotation, recorded to identify the exact codebase or package; for example a GitHub URL, Conda package source, or vendor distribution.
Reference library or knowledge base used to match processed features to alkaloid identities, recorded at annotation time; examples include an in-house alkaloid library, MassBank, GNPS, or HMDB.
Version or release date of the reference library used for alkaloid annotation, recorded at process time for reproducibility.
Mode used to match processed features to reference alkaloids, recorded during annotation; examples include exact mass, MS/MS spectral match, retention-time match, or combined evidence.

Maximum mass error tolerated when matching processed features to reference alkaloid identities, expressed in parts per million and recorded as an annotation parameter. Typical values may range from 1 to 20 ppm depending on platform.
Maximum retention-time deviation tolerated for alkaloid annotation, in minutes, recorded as a process parameter when retention time is used in matching.
Minimum confidence score or posterior probability required to assign an alkaloid identity, recorded during annotation; the scale depends on the software used.
Number of processed features assigned an alkaloid identity by the annotation process, recorded as a process outcome summary.
Qualitative assessment of whether the alkaloid annotation run produced usable identity assignments for downstream pathway analysis.

annotated_alkaloids.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only output properties of the annotated alkaloid table: file/table format, identity counts, chemical class summaries, confidence and ambiguity summaries, and quality indicators describing the final annotated result. I excluded annotation software, reference libraries, and matching thresholds because those belong to the upstream alkaloid_annotation Process node, and I excluded the processed feature table because that belongs upstream to processed_metabolite_features. I also avoided the already-generated collision fields and kept the schema focused on the annotated alkaloid artifact.

md_schema.descr: File or table format used to store the derived annotated alkaloid output, recorded when the artifact is written; examples include CSV, TSV, JSON, or Parquet.

Total number of rows in the derived annotated alkaloid table, counted after annotation and formatting. This may exceed the number of unique compounds if multiple adducts, isomers, or evidence records are listed.
Number of unique alkaloid identities represented in the derived table, counted from the final annotation artifact.
Number of distinct alkaloid classes represented in the derived table, such as indole, isoquinoline, quinoline, or pyrrolizidine classes, counted from the final output artifact.
Percentage of annotated alkaloid entries that meet the high-confidence identity threshold in the derived table, calculated from the final artifact as a summary quality indicator.
Percentage of annotated alkaloid entries retained as putative or tentative assignments rather than confirmed identities, calculated from the final output artifact.
Percentage of annotated alkaloid entries supported by MS/MS spectral evidence in the derived table, calculated from the final artifact.
Qualitative assessment of whether the derived annotated alkaloid table contains likely novel compounds or only known references, evaluated from the final output artifact.
Accession or internal identifier assigned to the derived annotated alkaloid table artifact, such as a repository release tag or internal table code.

integrative_pathway_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only integrative-analysis workflow details: analysis software/pipeline, version, repository, input harmonization, linkage rules, scoring thresholds, evidence weights, and a run-level QC outcome. I excluded upstream derivative contents such as the annotated gene, locus, and alkaloid tables, because those belong to their own nodes, and I excluded the downstream link table because that belongs to the alkaloid_biosynthesis_links derivative. I also avoided repeating fields already generated for earlier process nodes unless they are specific to the integration step.

md_schema.descr: Software or custom pipeline used to integrate genomic cluster annotations with chemically annotated alkaloids, recorded for this process step; for example a custom bioinformatics pipeline or network-analysis tool.
Version of the integration software or pipeline used in this process, recorded at run time for reproducibility; for example '1.0.0' or a workflow release tag.

Repository or implementation source used for the integrative pathway analysis, recorded to identify the exact codebase or package; for example a GitHub URL, Conda package source, or internal workflow repository.
Method used to harmonize gene-cluster, locus, and alkaloid tables before integration, recorded during the process; examples include ID mapping, ontology normalization, or manual curation.

Type of rule used to infer links between genomic clusters and alkaloid products, recorded as part of the integrative process; examples include co-occurrence, genomic proximity, biosynthetic logic, or evidence scoring.
Relative weight assigned to gene annotation evidence when inferring pathway relationships, recorded during integration. Use a normalized score or percent-like value consistent with the workflow.
Relative weight assigned to locus-mapping evidence when inferring pathway relationships, recorded during integration. Use a normalized score or percent-like value consistent with the workflow.
Relative weight assigned to alkaloid-annotation evidence when inferring pathway relationships, recorded during integration. Use a normalized score or percent-like value consistent with the workflow.
Minimum evidence score or confidence required to accept a biosynthetic pathway relationship during integration, recorded as a process parameter. The numeric scale depends on the integration model.
Number of genomic-to-chemical pathway links inferred by the integrative analysis process, recorded as a process outcome summary.
Qualitative assessment of whether the integrative pathway analysis produced usable links for downstream reporting, recorded at process completion.

alkaloid_biosynthesis_links.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only output properties of the integrative link table: file/record format, link counts, linked entity coverage, confidence summaries, evidence-composition summaries, and result-level quality indicators. I excluded integration software, weights, and thresholds because those belong to the upstream integrative_pathway_analysis Process node, and I excluded the individual upstream annotations because those belong to their own derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating already-generated identifiers and kept the schema focused on the final combined pathway-link artifact.

md_schema.descr: File or table format used to store the derived alkaloid biosynthesis link result, recorded when the artifact is written; examples include CSV, TSV, JSON, or Parquet.
Total number of inferred links between gene clusters, loci, and alkaloid products in the derived link table, counted from the final output artifact.
Number of unique biosynthetic gene clusters represented in the derived link table, counted from the final artifact.
Number of unique alkaloids represented in the derived link table, counted from the final artifact.
Number of unique genomic loci represented in the derived link table, counted from the final artifact.
Mean confidence score assigned to inferred biosynthetic pathway links in the derived table, calculated from the final integration output. The exact scale depends on the upstream integration method.
Percentage of inferred links in the derived table that meet the high-confidence threshold, calculated from the final artifact as a quality summary.

Compact summary of the evidence types contributing to the derived links, such as co-occurrence, genomic proximity, biosynthetic logic, or annotation support. Record the dominant or mixed evidence profile in the final artifact.
Qualitative assessment of whether the derived link table is suitable for interpretation and downstream reuse, evaluated on the final output artifact.
Accession or internal identifier assigned to the derived biosynthesis link table artifact, such as a repository release tag or internal link code.
